outcome: Server identity held as a portable profile, so a failed blade is replaced by applying a profile rather than rebuilding a machine.
overview: A hospital’s server estate accumulates: each clinical system arrives with its own hardware specification, its own build and its own person who knows it. UCS with Intersight separates the server’s identity — its firmware levels, boot configuration and network identity — from the physical hardware, so replacing a failed blade means applying a profile rather than rebuilding a machine. In a clinical estate the argument is recovery time rather than provisioning speed: how quickly a system comes back is what matters to the ward.

benefits.text: A server’s identity is a profile, so replacement hardware assumes it rather than being rebuilt
benefits.limits: Profile portability covers firmware, boot and network identity; the operating system and application still have to come from backup or from shared storage

benefits.text: Firmware levels across the estate are managed as policy instead of drifting per machine
benefits.limits: Clinical system vendors often certify specific firmware levels, which constrains how freely policy can be applied and must be checked per system

benefits.text: Provisioning a new clinical system is a profile application rather than a build project
benefits.limits: Only for systems whose vendor permits standardised infrastructure; appliance-style clinical systems are excluded and should be listed

residency: Servers and clinical data stay in the hospital data centre; Intersight management can be consumed as a service or deployed as an on-premises appliance where telemetry must not leave

notFor.situation: An estate already standardised on another vendor’s converged compute with its own management
notFor.why: Profile portability is a property of the management domain, and a second domain does not extend the first

notFor.situation: A small estate of a few standalone servers
notFor.why: The chassis and management overhead exceeds the benefit below a meaningful server count

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco data-centre implementation partner · Duration: 10–14 weeks to a domain with the first clinical system migrated, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor hardware and software support with a replacement term appropriate to clinical criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Assessment — server inventory, measured capacity, clinical vendor firmware constraints, facility limits
2) Design — workload classes, profile and firmware policy model, spare capacity and domain sizing
3) Build — fabric interconnects, chassis and servers, profiles and policies instantiated
4) Migrate and hand over — first clinical system on a profile, recovery exercise completed, operations handed over
deliverables: A server profile applied to spare hardware restores service within the time agreed at design
Firmware policy is scoped by workload class and respects each clinical system’s certified level
Spare capacity exists for every workload class, verified by inventory
effort: 10–14 weeks to a domain with the first clinical system migrated, hardware lead time excluded
